trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use this time to rest on the plane and prepare your arrival documents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at ACDMX airport at 13:00. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal Aérea station (very budget-friendly at ~$5 MXN) to the city center. Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico. Once settled, take a leisurely walk to the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Admire the exterior of the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace at no cost. Stroll through the surrounding streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street Madero, lined with historic buildings and street performers. Visit the Templo Mayor ruins (exterior view is free from the street). Wind down with a relaxed dinner near the Zócalo.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Head to Mercado de San Juan (about 10 min walk from hotel) for fresh tacos, quesadillas, or tortas from market stalls — expect to spend 80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD).
meals.dinner: Try a local taquería near the Zócalo such as Tacos de Canasta stands on Calle Uruguay or Calle 5 de Febrero — filling tacos for 15–20 MXN each. Budget: ~100–150 MXN (~$5–8 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize hydration and acclimatizing to Mexico City's high altitude (2,240m / 7,350 ft). Keep cash in small bills for street food and Metro rides. Metro fare is ~$5 MXN per ride — one of the cheapest transit systems in the world.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with breakfast at a local market. Then visit the Templo Mayor Museum (entry ~$85 MXN / ~$4 USD, free on Sundays) — an extraordinary Aztec archaeological site right in the heart of Centro Histórico. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ruins and museum exhibits detailing Aztec civilization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio de Bellas Artes (exterior is free; interior murals gallery entry ~$85 MXN). Marvel at the stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture. Afterward, head to the nearby Alameda Central park — a beautiful public garden that's completely free. Relax, people-watch, and soak in local life. Visit the Museo Mural Diego Rivera adjacent to the park (entry ~$45 MXN / ~$2 USD) to see Diego Rivera's famous mural 'Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in Alameda Park.'
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and explore the vibrant evening street food scene around Plaza Garibaldi, where Mariachi bands perform nightly (free to watch from the plaza). Enjoy the lively atmosphere of one of Mexico City's most iconic cultural spots.

meals.breakfast: Visit Mercado de San Juan or a local fondita (small family restaurant) near the hotel for chilaquiles or tamales with atole — budget ~80–100 MXN (~$4–5 USD).
meals.lunch: Grab lunch at a comida corrida (set lunch menu) restaurant near Bellas Artes — typically includes soup, main dish, rice, beans, and a drink for ~80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD). Look for handwritten signs saying 'Comida Corrida' in restaurant windows.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner near Plaza Garibaldi — try tostadas, gorditas, or elotes (corn on the cob with toppings). Budget ~100–130 MXN (~$5–7 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Many national museums are FREE on Sundays — if you can shuffle the itinerary, move museum visits to Sunday for maximum savings. Carry a small daypack and keep valuables secure in crowded areas. Comfortable walking shoes are essential — expect to walk 5–8 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 3) to Coyoacán, one of Mexico City's most charming and bohemian neighborhoods (~30 min ride). Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum — 'La Casa Azul' (The Blue House). Book tickets in advance online as they sell out quickly; entry ~$270 MXN (~$13 USD). This is the most significant splurge of the trip but absolutely worth it for culture lovers. Spend 1.5 hours exploring Frida's life, art, and the beautifully preserved home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the picturesque Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo in Coyoacán — free and full of local life, artisan vendors, and street performers. Browse the Mercado de Artesanías de Coyoacán for handmade crafts (browsing is free; souvenirs are very affordable). Walk to the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán for an authentic local market experience. Return to Centro Histórico via Metro in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the rooftop terrace bars near the Zócalo for sunset views (some have no cover charge with a drink minimum). Walk along Calle Regina, a lively pedestrianized street in Centro Histórico popular with locals, filled with cafes, bars, and street art.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local café near the hotel before heading out — try café de olla (traditional Mexican spiced coffee) with pan dulce (sweet bread). Budget ~60–80 MXN (~$3–4 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat lunch inside Mercado de Coyoacán — try the famous tostadas de tinga or enchiladas from market stalls. Budget ~100–150 MXN (~$5–8 USD). This is one of the best value food markets in the city.
meals.dinner: Back in Centro Histórico, try Café de Tacuba (a historic restaurant since 1912 on Calle Tacuba) for traditional Mexican cuisine at moderate prices — mole enchiladas or pozole. Budget ~180–250 MXN (~$9–13 USD) — a slight splurge but a cultural experience in itself.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance via their official website (museofridakahlo.org.mx). The Metro journey to Coyoacán requires a transfer — take Line 2 to Taxqueña or Line 3 to Viveros station. Coyoacán is very walkable once you arrive. Bring a light jacket as evenings can be cool in March.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Chapultepec (Line 1, Chapultepec station). Explore Bosque de Chapultepec — one of the largest urban parks in the Western Hemisphere and completely free to enter. Walk through the park, enjoy the lake area, and observe local families and joggers. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Castle) — entry ~$85 MXN (~$4 USD). The castle houses the Museo Nacional de Historia with stunning murals by Siqueiros and O'Gorman, and offers panoramic views of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the upscale Polanco neighborhood (free to explore) — a stark contrast to Centro Histórico, showcasing Mexico City's cosmopolitan side. Browse the Presidente Masaryk avenue (Mexico City's version of the Champs-Élysées) for window shopping. Visit the free outdoor sculpture garden at the Museo Soumaya plaza (the iconic silver building) — the exterior and plaza are free; interior entry is also free on certain days. Return to Centro Histórico via Metro.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Eje Central area for evening street food exploration. Check out the bookshop and cultural center El Péndulo or browse independent bookstores in the area. Enjoy a quiet evening stroll through the illuminated streets of Centro Histórico.

meals.breakfast: Try a local breakfast spot near the hotel for huevos rancheros or molletes (toasted bolillo with beans and cheese). Budget ~80–100 MXN (~$4–5 USD).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from a market (torta or tacos) to eat in Chapultepec Park — a classic local experience. Budget ~80–100 MXN (~$4–5 USD).
meals.dinner: Head to Mercado de San Juan for dinner — try fresh seafood tostadas, cheeses, or international food stalls for a unique market dinner experience. Budget ~120–160 MXN (~$6–8 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Chapultepec Park is very large — wear comfortable shoes. The park is busiest on weekends with locals; a Thursday visit means fewer crowds. Keep an eye on your belongings on the Metro during rush hours (7–9am and 5–8pm). The Polanco walk from Chapultepec is about 20 minutes on foot — enjoyable and scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) — one of the greatest museums in the world and an absolute must-see. Entry ~$85 MXN (~$4 USD), free on Sundays. Located inside Chapultepec Park (Metro: Chapultepec, Line 1). Dedicate a full 2–3 hours here — highlights include the Aztec Sun Stone (incorrectly called the 'Aztec Calendar'), Mayan artifacts, and exhibits covering all of Mexico's pre-Hispanic cultures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro Histórico for some last-minute exploration. Visit the Secretaría de Educación Pública (SEP building) on Calle Argentina — free entry to see Diego Rivera's incredible mural cycle covering three floors of the building's courtyards. One of the most underrated free art experiences in the city. Browse souvenir shops along Calle Moneda near the Zócalo for affordable handicrafts, textiles, and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening enjoying a farewell dinner at a traditional Mexican restaurant. Take one last walk around the Zócalo at night when the square is beautifully lit and the atmosphere is magical. Reflect on the trip over a final mezcal or agua fresca.

meals.breakfast: Splurge slightly on your last morning — visit a local café for a full Mexican breakfast with eggs, beans, tortillas, and fresh juice. Budget ~120–150 MXN (~$6–8 USD).
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and delicious lunch from street taco stands near the Anthropology Museum or back in Centro Histórico. Budget ~80–100 MXN (~$4–5 USD).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at El Cardenal (a beloved traditional Mexican restaurant near the Zócalo, known for authentic regional cuisine). Order the mole negro or chiles en nogada if in season. Budget ~250–350 MXN (~$13–18 USD) — a worthy splurge for the final night.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is on Day 6 (March 6), pack your bags tonight and confirm your airport transfer. The Metro to the airport from Centro Histórico takes approximately 45–60 minutes with one transfer — budget extra time for peak hours. Keep ~$200 MXN (~$10 USD) in cash for airport expenses. Overall trip tip: always carry a photocopy of your passport, use Metro over taxis for safety and savings, and don't miss trying agua de Jamaica (hibiscus water) and horchata from street vendors throughout your stay.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk through the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace from the outside. Stroll along Madero Street, a pedestrian boulevard lined with colonial architecture, street performers, and local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric streets of Centro Histórico as they light up at dusk. Visit the stunning Palacio de Bellas Artes exterior and the surrounding Alameda Central park for a relaxing evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: El Cardenal (Palma 23, Centro Histórico) — a beloved mid-range institution serving traditional Mexican cuisine including tamales, chiles en nogada, and house-made aguas frescas. Budget ~$15–20 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Taquería Los Cocuyos (Bolívar 56, Centro Histórico) — a legendary late-night taco stand just steps from the Zócalo. Try tacos de tripa, suadero, and cabeza. Budget ~$5–8 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 starts post-arrival. Keep the pace relaxed to recover from the flight. Centro Histórico is very walkable — comfortable shoes are a must. Be aware of altitude (2,240 m) and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its excellent on-site museum. This Aztec ruin sits at the heart of the city and offers incredible insight into pre-Hispanic civilization. Allow 2–2.5 hours. Open from 9:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's epic murals depicting Mexican history — free entry. Afterward, explore the nearby Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Jamaica for a sensory dive into local food culture, fresh produce, flowers, and street snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) nearby for a cultural curiosity, then settle into the lively Plaza Garibaldi to experience mariachi music performed live by competing bands — a quintessential Mexico City evening.

meals.breakfast: Café de Tacuba (Tacuba 28, Centro Histórico) — a historic café operating since 1912. Try the enchiladas, atole, and freshly baked pan dulce. Budget ~$8–12 USD per person.
meals.lunch: Street food tour around Mercado de la Merced — try tlayudas, quesadillas de flor de calabaza, and fresh fruit with chili and lime. Budget ~$5–8 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bar Montejo (near Plaza Garibaldi) — solid mid-range Mexican food with live music ambiance. Try cochinita pibil tacos and a Mexican craft beer. Budget ~$12–18 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor entry is approximately $5 USD. The Palacio Nacional is free. Plaza Garibaldi is most vibrant after 8 PM — keep valuables secure in busy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or an Uber to Coyoacán (~25 min from Centro). Explore the cobblestone streets, colorful colonial houses, and the famous Jardín Centenario. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Mercado de Coyoacán for lunch and local snacks. Afterward, visit the Leon Trotsky Museum nearby for a fascinating historical detour. Return to Centro Histórico in the late afternoon via Uber or metro.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Roma Norte / Colonia Juárez area (a short Uber ride from Centro) — browse boutique shops, street art, and trendy cafés before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Local panadería near your hotel — pick up fresh conchas, cuernos, and a café de olla for under $3 USD.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try tostadas de tinga, enfrijoladas, and fresh agua de jamaica. Budget ~$6–10 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Contramar (Durango 200, Colonia Roma) — one of Mexico City's most celebrated seafood restaurants. Try the signature tuna tostadas and grilled fish. Budget ~$20–28 USD per person. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets (~$14 USD) must be booked online at museofridakahlo.org.mx well in advance. Coyoacán is most enjoyable on weekdays when it's less crowded. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — depart early (by 8:30 AM) from Terminal Central del Norte via public bus (~1 hour, very affordable) or book a shared tour (~$25–35 USD including transport). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — visit the Temple of Quetzalcoatl and the on-site museum. Return to Mexico City by mid-afternoon. Rest at the hotel before heading out again.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively nightlife and culture of Colonia Roma or Condesa — visit a mezcalería for a curated mezcal tasting, a uniquely Mexican experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab tamales and atole from a street cart near the bus terminal before departure — a true local morning ritual. Budget ~$2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: La Gruta Restaurant at Teotihuacán — a dramatic restaurant set inside a natural cave near the ruins. Serves traditional Mexican dishes. Budget ~$15–22 USD per person. A memorable mid-range splurge.
meals.dinner: Merotoro (Amsterdam 204, Condesa) — a Baja-Mediterranean fusion restaurant with an excellent seasonal menu. Budget ~$18–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán entry is approximately $5 USD. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water — the site is fully exposed. Start early to beat heat and crowds. The site opens at 9:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec Park — one of the world's greatest museums, housing the Aztec Sun Stone and vast pre-Hispanic collections. Allow 2.5–3 hours. Take an Uber or metro (Chapultepec station) from Centro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's expansive urban park. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) for panoramic city views and Mexican imperial history exhibits. Head back to Centro Histórico for last-minute souvenir shopping around the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner celebration in Centro Histórico. Enjoy a rooftop bar with views of the illuminated Zócalo and Metropolitan Cathedral for a memorable send-off.

meals.breakfast: Expendio de Maíz Sin Nombre (Medellin 35, Roma Sur) — a celebrated breakfast spot serving heirloom corn-based dishes. Try the tlayuda and black bean tamales. Budget ~$10–15 USD per person.
meals.lunch: Street tacos and snacks in Chapultepec Park from local vendors — try elotes (grilled corn), chicharrón, and fresh-squeezed juice. Budget ~$4–6 USD.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico (Isabel la Católica 30, Centro Histórico) — an elegant courtyard restaurant specializing in refined regional Mexican cuisine. Try mole negro and chiles en nogada. Budget ~$20–28 USD per person. Perfect farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Museo Nacional de Antropología entry is approximately $5 USD (free on Sundays). La Ciudadela market is great for quality crafts, textiles, and Talavera pottery at fair prices. If departing the next morning, pack bags the night before and confirm transport to the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico via private luxury car service. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of Centro Histórico: explore the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), marvel at the Metropolitan Cathedral, and visit the Palacio Nacional to view Diego Rivera's iconic murals. Stroll through the atmospheric streets of the historic center with your expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset visit to the rooftop terrace of a nearby boutique hotel bar (such as the rooftop of Hotel Downtown México) for panoramic views of the illuminated Zócalo. Ease into your first evening with a mezcal cocktail and light bites.

meals.lunch: N/A — arrival at 13:00; light snack provided during hotel check-in welcome amenity
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azul Histórico (inside Hotel Downtown México) — celebrated Mexican cuisine in a stunning colonial courtyard setting. Try the slow-cooked lamb barbacoa and signature mole negro. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. The hotel concierge can assist with all reservations and guided tour bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Indulgent breakfast at the hotel, then a private guided visit to the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class museum — the ancient Aztec ceremonial center unearthed beneath the city. A knowledgeable archaeologist-guide brings the layers of history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Mercado de San Juan, a premium gourmet market beloved by chefs and food lovers, featuring artisan cheeses, imported delicacies, fresh seafood, and exotic local ingredients. Enjoy a curated tasting experience with a local food expert. Afterward, visit the nearby Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau architecture and muralist masterpieces.
day_by_day.evening: Private mezcal and tequila tasting experience at a curated mezcalería in Colonia Centro, learning about the terroir and production of Mexico's most iconic spirits from a certified sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Hotel in-house breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, chilaquiles, tamales, and specialty Mexican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet tasting lunch at Mercado de San Juan — curated selection of oysters, smoked fish, artisan cheeses, and local charcuterie paired with natural wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar (short ride to Colonia Roma) — legendary Mexico City seafood institution. Must-try: tuna tostadas and the signature grilled red snapper with two salsas. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — confirm opening hours. Contramar fills up quickly; have the concierge book at least 2–3 days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Coyoacán neighborhood for a morning immersion in bohemian culture. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) with a skip-the-line private tour, followed by a leisurely walk through Coyoacán's cobblestone streets, colorful colonial buildings, and charming central plaza.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the greatest anthropology museums on Earth. A private guide will curate a 2-hour highlights tour covering Aztec, Maya, and pre-Columbian civilizations. Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's grand urban park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a leisurely evening. Attend a classical music performance or cultural event at Palacio de Bellas Artes (check program in advance), then enjoy a late dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café El Jarocho in Coyoacán — an iconic local coffee institution serving traditional café de olla and pan dulce
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Cardenal (Coyoacán branch or Centro location) — a prestigious institution for traditional Mexican cuisine; try the classic caldo tlalpeño soup and carnitas
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol — Chef Enrique Olvera's globally acclaimed flagship restaurant. The omakase-style tasting menu celebrates the evolution of Mexican cuisine. One of Latin America's top restaurants. Essential reservation.

day_by_day.notes: Pujol reservations should be made weeks or even months in advance — have your travel agent or hotel concierge secure this booking before the trip. Museo Frida Kahlo also requires advance tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán, approximately 50 km northeast of the city. Depart early by private luxury vehicle. Enjoy a private archaeologist-led tour of the Pyramid of the Sun, Pyramid of the Moon, and the Avenue of the Dead before the crowds arrive. Sunrise or early morning light at the site is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey stops at a traditional pulque hacienda for a tasting of Mexico's ancient agave beverage. Visit a local obsidian artisan workshop to see traditional pre-Columbian craftsmanship. Return to the hotel by mid-afternoon for rest and refresh.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric streets of Centro Histórico by night on a private evening culture walk — visit illuminated landmarks, hidden baroque churches, and the spectacular light show at the Zócalo. End the evening with cocktails at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast prepared by the hotel — freshly baked pastries, fruit, and thermos coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Gruta restaurant, Teotihuacán — a spectacular restaurant set inside a natural cave adjacent to the archaeological zone. Enjoy traditional Mexican dishes in a truly unique setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Limosneros in Centro Histórico — innovative pre-Hispanic cuisine using ancient ingredients like huitlacoche, escamoles (ant larvae), and chapulines (grasshoppers) in refined contemporary preparations

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 7:00–7:30 AM for Teotihuacán to beat crowds and midday heat. Wear comfortable walking shoes and sun protection. The site involves significant walking and stair climbing.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in or enjoy a slow breakfast at the hotel. Visit the nearby Mercado de Artesanías or the upscale Fonart government craft store for premium Mexican artisan souvenirs: Talavera ceramics, silver jewelry, embroidered textiles, and alebrijes. Browse the antiquarian bookshops and galleries along Avenida Madero.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class with a celebrated local chef — learn to prepare three iconic Mexican dishes from scratch, including handmade tortillas, a classic mole, and a traditional dessert. Classes are held in a beautifully appointed kitchen in the Centro area and include a curated mezcal pairing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Mexico City's most iconic fine-dining establishments, followed by a nightcap at a world-class cocktail bar in the Juárez or Roma neighborhood to toast the end of an extraordinary journey.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — huevos rancheros, fresh juices, and Mexican hot chocolate
meals.lunch: Light lunch included as part of the cooking class experience — enjoy the dishes you prepared with your chef
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Quintonil — Chef Jorge Vallejo's acclaimed restaurant celebrating modern Mexican cuisine with hyper-local and seasonal ingredients. Exceptional tasting menu with wine pairing. A true culinary farewell to Mexico City.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange private airport transfer through the hotel concierge. Quintonil and Pujol are often considered interchangeable as Mexico City's top two restaurants — if Pujol was secured for Day 3, Quintonil is the perfect finale. Pack purchases carefully, especially fragile ceramics.
